marta (eng-ml): quick dump from today's quant experiments on zephyr9b. ran fp16 / int6 / int4 variants across the usual slices. looking for a short recommendation for GTN defaults + canary plan.
jin (ml): please drop the scorecard & major regressions.
marta (eng-ml): pasted perf/quality summary (aggregate smoke on 8k sampled requests, plus eval sets):
```
model: zephyr9b-v2-2026-04
variants: fp16, int6, int4
throughput (tokens/sec): fp16 260, int6 310, int4 370
latency p50/p95 (ms): fp16 38/98, int6 46/140, int4 58/260
cost per 1k tokens: fp16 $0.0016, int6 $0.0010, int4 $0.00068
quality (exact match / avg BLEU): fp16 89.7 / 42.1, int6 89.2 / 41.8, int4 87.4 / 40.6
notes: int4 gives ~32% token cost reduction vs int6 but p95 latency doubles on long sequences. int4 shows concentrated quality drops on instruction-following and code-gen slices.
```
ella (prod): that int4 quality loss is concerning for code-gen customers. any regression >2 EM anywhere?
marta (eng-ml): yes - on code generation prompts (multi-file synthesis style) avg EM drop ~3.1 vs fp16; instruction-following prompt set sees ~1.8 drop. Chat/short-qa slices are within 0.6 EM. Rerank unaffected.
jin (ml): interestingly, int6 is pretty close to fp16 across most slices. tradeoff summary: int6 = safe middle ground (20-30% cheaper than fp16), int4 = huge cost savings but risky for high-fidelity tasks.
vic (gtn): product take: many GTN customers default to chat and short answers. Could we expose a per-route knob (quality-tier: high/standard/eco) and map high->fp16, standard->int6, eco->int4?
ella (prod): that's workable but we should limit eco (int4) to opt-in with clear caveats. also need routing defaults for new tenants.
marta (eng-ml): operational plan I'm proposing:
- default: standard (int6) for new GTN tenants
- high-quality routes (code-gen, legal, medical): force fp16 by route config
- eco tier: opt-in only, disabled for managed GTN tenants unless customer acknowledges quality delta
- canary: 48h at 15% traffic, distributed across slices, with probes and auto-fallback to fp16 or int6 depending on slice
- probes: 200 chat prompts, 60 code-gen tasks, 40 instruction-follow. probe cadence every 10m during canary
- triggers: revert if any probe category shows >1.5 EM regression sustained for 30m OR error rate spike >0.5%

jin (ml): I can own the probe sets and compute live delta metrics. also add a qualitative human review channel for code-gen samples every 2h during canary.
ellA (prod): typo on my name :) +1 to human review for code-gen. also include a product-facing advisory doc.
ops-bot: canary-rule created: id=canner-3421, start=2026-04-12T09:00:00Z, traffic=15%, fallback=fp16/int6 (per-slice mapping), alert-channel=#eng-ml-ops
vic (gtn): for GTN onboarding copy: "Default: int6 (standard). High-quality routes pinned to fp16. Eco (int4) is opt-in only; recommend for throughput-only workloads where code-gen/instruction fidelity is not required." will draft and post.\marta (eng-ml): additional engineering notes: caching and prefix warmstart reduce int4 latency tail by ~30% on long sequences in local tests; could mitigate some p95 concerns but not quality. recommended engineering follow-ups: 1) test prefix-KV caching on long instruction flows 2) run larger scale int4 eval on recent customer prompts 3) consider hybrid routing (start int4 then upgrade to int6 after 512 tokens) as an experiment.
jin (ml): hybrid routing idea is neat; we should simulate delta with our replay infra before canary.
marta (eng-ml): decision summary: we will proceed with canary using int6 as the default standard, reserve fp16 for high-quality routes, and keep int4 behind opt-in/experiment. action items assigned: jin -> probe dashboard & replay sim; ella -> product advisory draft; vic -> GTN config mapping; marta -> rollout checklist + prefetched cache experiment.
ella (prod): will coordinate customer comms for opt-in eco tier.
vic (gtn): thanks team. please ping when canary starts.
marta (eng-ml): closing thread 1: will follow up with canary results and the replay sim output.
